requirements.where: Appendix A: STK files and settings

technical_issues.issue: 510 s of 771 s is about 66%, not 60%. The stated 34 min/day corresponds to 60% of 57 min, so the contact-time figure is inconsistent with the cited fraction (66% gives about 38 min).
Downlink time labelled as 34 minutes, but 2,000 s is 33.3 minutes. Small rounding inconsistency feeding the 3.5× margin.
Daily imaging of one 60 km × 1,000 km strip is asserted without justification against 14.9 orbits per day and the 5-day revisit claim. The 4:1 compression ratio is also unreferenced.
Eclipse duration of 34 min is asserted, not derived from the 08:45 node time or beta angle. It is close to the worst-case value, so the battery sizing claim is unsupported.
Figure 2 caption gives no source or credit, though the plot appears to come from an external or MATLAB model, breaching the citation requirement (R11).
Lifetime estimate H/rate assumes a constant decay rate, but drag accelerates as altitude falls, so 2.2 and 32-year figures are only rough order-of-magnitude values, not stated as such.

overall: Strong, well-organised report that addresses every requirement with checkable calculations; key orbit, drag and access results verify. Marks are reduced for numerical inconsistencies (contact fraction, downlink time), an unjustified daily-imaging assumption, an eclipse figure without derivation, an unsourced figure, and several uncited statements.
